newsitem.title: DUBAI: TENNIS-MOYA SUFFERS FIRST ROUND LOSS TO NOVAK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MOYA SUFFERS FIRST ROUND LOSS TO NOVAK.

text.p: Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya stumbled in the first round of the $1 million Dubai Open tennis tournament on Wednesday, losing 6-2 0-6 5-7 to Czech Jiri Novak.
The Spaniard, feeling physically and mentally drained, admitted he was not in the right frame of mind against Novak.
"I had no time to relax (mentally) since the Australian Open and the Davis Cup match against Germany," Moya, ranked ninth in the world, said.

"The two tournaments put a lot of pressure on me and I knew it would take its toll. But this doesn't mean Novak won because I played badly. He won the game because he played much better and kept improving.
"I had a chance in the third set when I served 5-4 but Novak, whom I had beaten a couple of times before, handled the pressure well.
"My ultimate dream is to win at Wimbledon but I still have a lot to learn."
Boris Becker, beaten by Moya in the first round of his Australian Open defence, made a winning start in Dubai.
Seventh-seeded Becker overcame a determined challenge from fellow German Kevin Goellner 6-2 6-7 (5-7) 6-2.
Becker, ranked 13th in the world, has been out of the tournament picture since the Australian Open and missed last weekend's German Davis Cup defeat against Spain.
"When you are playing after some time, winning the first always gives you confidence as it did to me today," he said.
Becker felt "we were not pushing each other too much. I tended to be a little less aggressive which allowed him to bounce back. But things were okay for me in the decider.
"If I stay healthy and focused -- the key to success -- I can carry on well for some time more," the Grand Slam Cup winner said.
Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek survived a brave challenge from Indian wild card entry Leander Paes, dropping the first set before winning 5-7 6-4 6-2.
The Dutchman had to fight all the way against adventurous Olympic bronze medallist Paes, who needed treatment for a muscle injury in the final set and then lost three games in succession.
Australia's former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash celebrated his first main draw singles victory since 1995 by beating Spain's Carlos Costa 7-6 (7-4) 7-6 (8-6).
